groups.heading: If you need help right now
groups.intro: Free, confidential and open around the clock.

entries.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
entries.note: For anyone in crisis, not only someone who is suicidal.

entries.name: Crisis Text Line
entries.note: Trained counsellors by text, if a call is not safe or possible.

entries.name: The Trevor Project
entries.note: Crisis support for LGBTQ young people.

entries.name: Trans Lifeline
entries.note: Peer support run by trans people. It does not call the police on a caller.

entries.name: National Runaway Safeline
entries.note: For a young person who has run, is thinking about it, or has been thrown out.

entries.name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
entries.note: Sexual assault support, including assault that happened years ago.

groups.heading: Reporting abuse in a program
groups.intro: A report can go to more than one place at once, and usually should. The bodies that can act are different in every state, and they do not talk to each other reliably.

entries.name: Where to report, state by state
entries.note: Every state and DC: the board that holds the therapist's licence, the agency that licenses the program, the legal and law enforcement channels, and the oversight bodies with a right to investigate. Each entry says what that body can actually do, whether it takes an anonymous report, and the day somebody last checked the number.

entries.name: Childhelp National Child Abuse Hotline
entries.note: Counselors around the clock. They will talk through what happened and work out which state agency takes the report, if you would rather start there than with a form.

groups.heading: For families: alternatives to a placement
groups.intro: Care that keeps a young person at home or with family, instead of sending them away.

entries.name: Wraparound basics
entries.note: The National Wraparound Initiative at Portland State University on wraparound: a team built around the young person and family, working in the community rather than in a facility.

entries.name: Kinship care facts
entries.note: ACH Child and Family Services on placing a child with relatives, and why children do better there than with strangers.

entries.name: Unsilenced: safer alternatives
entries.note: Evidence-based treatment for young people with mental health needs, and what to look for in it.

groups.heading: Taking legal action
groups.intro: What a survivor needs to know before looking for a lawyer.

entries.name: A Survivor's Guide to Legal Action Against Troubled Teen Industry Programs
entries.note: By Shannon Saul. Statutes of limitation, what evidence matters, and what to expect. PDF.

entries.name: Five Facts About the Troubled Teen Industry
entries.note: The American Bar Association, for a lawyer who has not worked one of these cases before.

entries.name: ABA Resolution 605: the Troubled Teen Industry and Institutional Child Abuse
entries.note: The American Bar Association's 2023 policy backing the Stop Institutional Child Abuse Act and laws against abusive practices in youth residential programs.
